name: vLLM's query_marlin_supported_quant_types returns [] below compute capability 75 and SGLang's identical-named function returns [] below 80, so on Turing the two engines disagree about whether Marlin exists
symptom: The same AWQ or GPTQ checkpoint on the same Turing GPU (T4, RTX 20-series) is served by a Marlin kernel in vLLM and by something else — Triton W4A16, or an error — in SGLang. Any statement of the form 'Marlin supports X' is ambiguous unless it names the engine.
root_cause: Two functions with the same name and nearly the same body. vLLM marlin_utils.py: `if not current_platform.is_rocm(): ... if device_capability < 75: return []`. SGLang marlin_utils.py: `if device_capability < 80: return []`. Both then return [uint4] for zero-point quant types and [uint4b8, uint8b128] plus optionally float8_e4m3fn and float4_e2m1f for symmetric ones. Note also that the FP4 and FP8 Marlin variants are looser than either in both engines: vLLM's is_fp8_marlin_supported() is just has_device_capability(75) and is_fp4_marlin_supported() is is_cuda() and has_device_capability(75).
workaround: State the engine whenever the Marlin floor is quoted. Do not carry '75' or '80' as a property of Marlin — it is a property of an engine's copy of the Marlin gate. For a Turing target, verify per engine rather than assuming parity.
notes: This sharpens an existing verified negative rather than contradicting it. [[quantization/qhw-vllm-kernel-capability-matrix]] records 'Volta has no Volta path: query_marlin_supported_quant_types() returns an EMPTY LIST when device_capability < 75'. That holds for vLLM on current main. This record adds that the negative is engine-scoped, and that the two engines disagree at the 75-79 band. Both re-read 2026-10-05.
